title: Constant-scalar bilinearity of integral derived internal Hom

from.place: Internal Hom is the derived closed internal Hom. The assigned Lean rational internal-Hom construction requires its integral action to be linear in each morphism argument.

statement: Fix a prime l, a finite extension E of Q_l with valuation ring O_E [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and a scheme W. Let H be the ambient integralDerivedInternalHom of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations], equipped with the published constant O_E action [lem-weil-integral-constructible-linear]. For any four ambient derived objects M, M′, N, N′ there exists an O_E-bilinear map Hom(M′,M) x Hom(N,N′) -> Hom(H(M,N),H(M′,N′)) whose value on (a,b) is exactly H.map(a.op,b). No boundedness, constructibility, completeness or flatness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Section Internal hom in the derived category (Tag 08J7), the preceding Hom-complex construction, and lemma-RHom-well-defined (Tag 0A95). Constant-scalar arrow calculation written by J1.

proof.text: Use the existing coefficientModuleLinear constant-section action on module sheaves. Compare its standard Mathlib derived linear structure (localization through Qh) with the published integralCoefficientLinear. The latter is uniquely characterized by integralScalarDerivedAction. The equality coefficientDerived_eq and CatCenter.ext_of_localization reduce comparison of the two central scalar actions to Q.map(r times identity)=r times identity. Linearity of Q proves this equality. Hence the two Linear structures, and therefore all their Hom modules, agree.

The already-proved generic tensor_linear helper in LineEvaluationInversePair is stated for an arbitrary module sheaf P, with no local-freeness hypothesis: it checks scalar linearity of tensorRight P on sheafified pure tensors. Restrict this global-section action along coefficient_scalarSections. Braiding gives linearity of tensorLeft P. Apply DerivedCategory.monoidalLinear to the native derived tensor. Thus that tensor is additive and linear in both variables for the standard derived action, and the scalar-structure equality in the first step identifies it with the published action.

Take the existing closedAdjunction for derivedInternalHomOfUniverses, with its monoidal structure equal to the native derived tensor. For precomposition H(f.op,id), apply the injective inverse adjunction Hom equivalence; evaluation_naturality identifies its transpose with tensorLeft(H(M,N)).map(f) followed by evaluation. Additivity and scalar linearity of tensor give the two first-variable laws. For postcomposition H(id,g), the right-adjoint-additive theorem gives additivity. Inverse transposition and naturality of the adjunction counit identify its transpose with evaluation followed by g, which gives scalar linearity. These are genuine separate linear maps on arbitrary derived arrows, not only chain representatives.

Compose the first-variable linear map with the second-variable linear map using bilinear composition in the ambient linear category. Linear.leftComp and LinearMap.comp give the inner linear map; additivity and scalar linearity of the outer map follow from the first-variable map and composition. Functor.map_comp identifies the composite H(f.op,id) followed by H(id,g) with the prescribed H.map(f.op,g). Specialize the generic private closedHom_bilinear proof to integralDerivedInternalHom, which is definitionally the recorded derivedInternalHomOfUniverses.

proof_origin.place: Section 08J7, equation-internal-hom and Lemma 08J9: reuse the existing native derived tensor-Hom adjunction; scalar linearity follows from tensor linearity and evaluation naturality.

lean.statement:
theorem integralDerivedHom_bilinear (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime]
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E]
    (W : Scheme.{u})
    (M M' N N' : DerivedCategory (integralTowerModules l E W)) :
    ∃ b : (M' ⟶ M) →ₗ[Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers l E]
        (N ⟶ N') →ₗ[Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers l E]
        ((integralDerivedInternalHom l E W).obj (op M, N) ⟶
          (integralDerivedInternalHom l E W).obj (op M', N')),
      ∀ a b', b a b' = (integralDerivedInternalHom l E W).map (Prod.mkHom a.op b')
